title: Rupee ends a tad higher as oil slide, foreign inflows lift sentiment
description: The Indian rupee experienced a slight boost this week, driven by declining oil prices and the prospect of increased foreign investment. Although initial gains were curtailed due to importer demand, the currency received support as short-seller positions diminished. Investors are keenly awaiting US inflation figures, as these may impact future interest rate strategies. Notably, Indian financial markets will be closed on Friday in observance of a holiday.

title: Housing sales rise 19% in Apr-Jun across 9 cities despite global uncertainties
description: Despite facing global economic challenges, Indian housing sales posted a staggering 19% increase, exceeding 1.12 lakh units from April to June. PropEquity data highlights significant demand in key urban centers including Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Navi Mumbai. Moreover, a notable 43% uptick in new property supply reflects growing market optimism, driven by solid domestic demand and economic resilience, even in the face of geopolitical tensions.

title: Sensex closes 109 points higher, Nifty above 24,050; IndiGo, M&M among top gainers
description: Indian stock markets closed with modest gains on Sensex monthly expiry day, as both indices erased significant intraday advances.  Sensex added 109 points to 77,100.47, and Nifty 50 climbed 34 points to 24,056.  Strong performances from IndiGo, M&M, and Maruti Suzuki bolstered the gains, while Power Grid shares saw notable declines.  The broader market, however, dipped into the red.

title: Nifty headed to 24,500 next week, says Dharmesh Shah; these 2 stocks are top buys right now
description: Indian equity markets are poised for further gains, with Nifty eyeing 24,500, according to ICICI Direct's Dharmesh Shah.  He highlights falling crude oil prices and rupee stability as key drivers. Bank Nifty has also shown strength, targeting 59,300.  Shah recommends buying dips and identifies Mahindra & Mahindra and Larsen & Toubro as top stock picks with clear upside potential.

title: Can Vedanta Aluminium, NALCO shares crash up to 40%? Why InCred sees major downside
description: InCred Equities has turned bearish on the aluminium sector, advising investors to exit aluminium stocks as it sees a potential 30–40% downside. The brokerage argues that the market is incorrectly valuing aluminium as a supply-constrained primary metal, overlooking its unique nature as a highly recyclable, above-ground resource.

title: India's CDMO industry set for global shift as pharma diversifies beyond China: Sai Life Sciences
description: Indian contract manufacturers are poised for significant growth as global pharmaceutical giants diversify away from China.  Companies like Sai Life Sciences are investing heavily in capacity, anticipating a surge in demand.  While regulatory processes mean benefits will be gradual, this supply-chain realignment presents a landmark opportunity for India's CDMO sector, with major players already strengthening partnerships.

title: EY, KPMG, Deloitte among top 10 auditors by number of companies audited in FY26
description: India’s audit market in FY26 remained dominated by large firms, with EY, KPMG and Deloitte leading by audit volume and market capitalisation exposure. Concentration persists, with limited firms handling multiple mandates, while auditor exits and tenure completions signal ongoing churn within the listed companies’ audit ecosystem.

title: India at start of a major recovery, foreign investors just beginning to return, says BlackRock's Ben Powell
description: India's equity markets are poised for a significant rebound as foreign investors begin to re-evaluate the nation's growth prospects. BlackRock's Ben Powell highlights normalizing oil prices and a broader recognition of India's long-term potential as key drivers. He believes the current recovery is in its nascent stages, with valuations presenting a compelling opportunity for early investors.

title: 13 BSE 500 stocks surged up to 200% in just 3 months; 3 turned multibaggers

title: Madhusudan Kela-backed fund buys stake in IPO-bound Steamhouse India for Rs 40 crore
description: Ace investor Madhusudan Kela's funds, along with Niveshaay Sambhav Fund, have injected Rs 49.99 crore into Steamhouse India via a pre-IPO placement. This strategic investment positions these entities to hold nearly 3% of the company's pre-IPO equity. Steamhouse India, a Surat-based firm, operates a unique centralized steam supply model for industries and is preparing for its initial public offering.
